properties.foundation_analysis: Bedrock comprises Carboniferous Lower Oil-Shale sedimentary strata overlain by glacial till. Superstructure lithics utilize local blonde Craigleith and grey Hailes sandstone. Mortar consists of traditional hot-mixed calcitic hydraulic lime with coarse river sand. Subterranean drainage slopes south towards the Water of Leith valley.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Bordering parkland belt featuring mature *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm), and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). Phenological state for late September: dense full-volume foliage displaying early autumnal chlorosis, lime-green shifts, and patchy leaf margin yellowing.

properties.architectural_summary:
Left: Victorian residential terrace, three storeys over raised basement, rectified vertical plane. Ashlar facade with canted bay windows, molded architraves, projecting stone cornices, and timber-framed sash-and-case fenestration. 
Center: Gothic Revival church structure with square multi-stage tower, stepped buttresses, decorative corner pinnacles, crenellated parapets, and pointed-arch lancet windows. Pitched roofs clad in Scottish slate. 
Right/Boundary: Low dressed sandstone dwarf retaining wall with copings flanking the garden perimeter.
